How do I know if this AI course and ML course is for me? This Post Graduate Program in AI and Machine Learning is for you if you are: - Data Scientist or Senior Data Analyst: If you are comfortable with data wrangling, have implemented statistical or machine learning models in the past, or have any prior experience as a working professional. You should also have some experience with R/Python/Scala. - Statistician: If you received formal education in statistics or mathematics or have any prior working experience. - Data Engineer/Big Data Engineer: If you have any prior experience in creating data pipelines/handling data warehouses and have created ETL procedures. In addition, you should be familiar with various frameworks and tools like Hadoop and Spark. - Software Developer: If you have prior experience creating and deploying software/apps, you are comfortable with object-oriented programming and know C/C++/Java/Python or a similar language. 2 . How will this course on artificial intelligence benefit me? This PG Diploma in AI aims to make you industry-ready and ensure that the learning outcomes are successfully achieved. Moreover, prior experience is another factor that determines the value of the Post Graduate Programme in AI & ML. Data Scientist or Senior Data Analyst: The AI PG courses will familiarise you with the advancements in ML and AI. It will also help you understand the mathematics behind algorithms and how you can modify them to suit your needs so that you can transition to a Senior Data Science or Machine Learning role. Statistician/Mathematician: Apart from familiarising you with the advancements in AI and machine Learning, the PG Diploma in AI & ML will help you understand how to define a structured approach to solve a business problem and equip you with the right tools so that you can transition to a Machine Learning or Data Science role. Data Engineer/Big Data Engineer: The PG Diploma in Machine Learning and AI will set up a solid foundation in Statistics, Machine Learning, and AI, along with problem-solving skills so that you can solve enterprise-level problems. It will build upon your existing knowledge of various tools to make you a Full-Stack Machine Learning or Data Science professional. Software Developer: Post graduation in AI and ML will help you create a strong foundation of Statistics, Machine Learning, and Business Understanding. It will leverage your existing knowledge of programming and expand the technologies you are familiar with so that you can become a well-rounded Machine Learning professional. 3 . What is this course on artificial intelligence and machine learning intended to do? This Post Graduate Diploma in AI and ML intends to produce extremely well-rounded data scientists and AI professionals with deep knowledge of mathematics, expertise in relevant tools/languages, and an understanding of cutting-edge algorithms and applications. With Post Graduation in AI and ML , you can learn skills and tools that are relevant and highly applicable in the current industry as artificial intelligence learning and applicability is at its peak. 4 . What can I expect out of these courses in artificial intelligence and machine learning? This program is considered among the top PG in Machine Learning programs and is designed for working professionals looking to pick up skills in advanced concepts like Reinforcement Learning, Graphical Models, NLP, and Deep Learning along with a solid foundation in Statistics. This Post Graduate Program in AI and Machine Learning demands consistent work and time commitment over the entire duration of 13 months. This is the reason why it is considered among the best PG program in AI and Machine Learning . 5 . What should I NOT expect from this programme? This PG Diploma in AI and ML aims to develop professionals who can be absorbed into Senior Data Scientist and Machine Learning/AI roles. The PG Program in Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning offered by IIIT Bangalore aims to facilitate the transition of professionals to the Machine Learning field. 6 . This PG Diploma in AI will make sure that the quality parameter of your learning remains high. 7 . Is there any deferral or refund policy for this programme? Refund Policy: (Programmes with prep-session component) You can claim a refund for the amount paid towards the Post Graduate Program in AI and Machine Learning at any time, before the Program Start Date, by visiting [www.upgrad.com](http://www.upgrad.com/) and submitting your refund form via the "My Application" section under your profile. You can request your Admissions Counselor to help you in applying and withdrawing for a refund by sending them an email with the reasons listed. The prep login will be activated immediately post-completion of the 'payment of the 1st block amount (caution money)' or on the 'Specified date' as communicated by upGrad. A processing fee of ₹10,000 will be levied in case a refund is claimed. The student has to pay the full fee within 7 days of payment of the block amount or cohort start date, whichever is earlier; otherwise, the admission letter will be rescinded, and a processing fee of INR 10,000 will be levied. Once the student pays the block amount, "any" refund shall be subject to a deduction of INR 10,000 processing charges. Any taxes paid by the student shall not be refundable, and the amount to be withheld will be higher than taxes paid or INR 10,000 processing fees. There shall be no refund applicable once the PG Diploma in Machine Learning and Artificial Intelligence has started. This is applicable even for those students who could not complete their payment and could not be enrolled in the batch opted for. However, the student can avail of pre-deferral as per the policy defined below for the same. Refund shall be processed to an eligible student within 30 working days from the date of receipt of the refund form from him/her in this regard. Refund shall be subject to a deduction of INR 10,000 processing charges or the GST paid, whichever is higher, as mentioned above. 1st Deferral (pre or post-program commencement) is free for all enrolled students with the following conditions: The Executive Post Graduate Diploma in AI and ML learners should complete the course in a maximum duration of 3 years from the initial batch start date. The Advanced Certificate Program learners should complete the course in a maximum duration of 2 years from the initial batch start date. 2nd deferral will be charged as explained below. 2nd Deferral Policy: (Post Programme Commencement) If a student is facing severe issues in dedicating time to the course, we provide the opportunity for the student to defer to another batch. A student can request for deferral only once and from the batch start date of the initial batch the student enrolled for. The student will be required to pay a deferral fee of 10% of the total course amount fee + Taxes, if any, along with the differential program fees between the two cohorts. The deferral request will be approved once the deferral fee is paid. Till this is completed, the student will be assumed to be continuing in the same cohort. The student has 7 days (including holidays and weekends) from the date of the deferral request to make the payment of the deferral fee, post which the deferral request will expire, and the student will continue as part of the current cohort. If the student completes the deferral payment, the student's login will be disabled, the student will leave the deferred cohort, and the student will start learning in the new cohort from the point of the last assignment that was graded in the deferred cohort. All grades and progress until that point will be carried forward as it is to the new cohort. For clarification, the grades of the graded assignments will be carried forward, whether or not the student had submitted these grades during the initial stage. The deferral can only be requested during the batch for which the student has enrolled is ongoing. Once the batch has been completed, deferral requests shall not be entertained. For clarification, the batch completion here shall mean the "last grace deadline", as communicated by upGrad., 2nd Deferral Policy: (Pre Programme Commencement) If a student, due to unavoidable circumstances, is unable to commence with the cohort and requests for a deferral before the cohort starts, we provide the opportunity for the student to defer to another cohort. To do so, the student will be required to pay 50% of the total Programme fee amount (inclusive of taxes) before the deferral can be approved. Till this is completed, the student will be assumed to be continuing in the same cohort. A student can request for deferral to any of the cohorts starting in the next 3 months from the start date of the initial batch in which the student was originally enrolled. For the first deferral request, subject to point no. 2 of the Pre-Programme Deferral Policy, no additional charges shall be levied. If a student wants to defer his enrolment a second time, such a student will have to make an additional payment of Rs.10,000 as a Deferral fee, and this amount shall be non-refundable under any circumstances. Once this payment is done, students will be eligible to defer to any of the cohorts starting in the next 3 months from the current cohort. The student has time till the current cohort launch date to make the payment of the balance 50% Programme fee, post which the deferral request will expire. Once the deferral window expires and if such a student wants to withdraw his or her enrolment from the said Programme, the refund policy will be applicable. The student shall be liable to pay the differential Programme fees between the two cohorts if any. 8 . Which banks allow using 0% Credit card EMI or Credit card EMI? To enrol in the PG Diploma in Machine Learning and AI , YOU have to go through the below-mentioned process- STEP-1: Online Eligibility Test Fill out an application and take a 40-minute online test with 18 questions to assess your aptitude: 10 questions from mathematics, aptitude & reasoning & 8 questions from programming. STEP-2: Review and Shortlisting of Suitable Candidates Our faculty for PG in Artificial Intelligence will review all applications, considering your educational and professional background, and review the test scores where applicable. Following this, offer letters will be rolled out so you are assured a great peer group to learn and network with. STEP-3: Enrollment for Access to Prep Content Make a quick block payment with assistance from our loan partners where required, receive immediate access to the content and begin your upGrad journey 14 . What key components and focus areas are covered in a PG Diploma in Machine Learning program? This 1-year PG Diploma in Machine Learning by IIIT Bangalore offers 360-degree expertise in Natural Language Processing (NLP), Deep Learning, Computer Vision, BERT, and more. You also learn in-demand Generative AI skills and tools like ChatGPT, Midjurney, GANs, and GNN. With a PG in Machine Learning , you can build real-world systems and take your career in ML to the next level. 15 . Can you provide insights into the specific curriculum and advantages of pursuing a PG Diploma in AI and ML? This PG Diploma in AI and ML has over 600 hours of learning materials across advanced modules like NLP, MLOps, transformers, and GANs. In this post graduate program in AI and machine learning , you can implement generative AI using Dall-E and ChatGPT in machine learning projects. The advantages of pursuing this PG Diploma in Machine Learning and Artificial Intelligence are accelerated career growth, higher salaries, leadership roles, global mobility, and opportunities to drive innovation. 16 . Tell me more about the differences between post-graduation in AI and ML and a specialised PG Diploma in the same field. While a full Post graduation in AI and ML provides extensive theoretical knowledge covering statistics, algebra, programming, and cloud engineering, a PG Diploma in Machine Learning offers accelerated speciality training in applied areas like computer vision systems, predictive analytics, ChatGPT integration, etc. A post graduate diploma in AI and ML is shorter in duration and is especially beneficial for working professionals. 17 . What sets apart a post-graduate diploma in AI and ML from other postgraduate programs in the tech industry? IIIT-B's PG Diploma in Machine Learning is created in collaboration with industry leaders, and its curriculum is co-designed with renowned tech firms. This helps you gain in-demand like GANs, NLP, etc., which align with current industry needs. Also, the PG in Artificial Intelligence program by IIIT-B focuses on working directly on AI systems rather than only theoretical concepts, which gives you an advantage. This is why it is the best PG program in AI and Machine Learning. 18 . How do admissions criteria and program structures vary among institutions offering a PG Diploma in AI? Admissions criteria are quite similar - most colleges want 50%+ bachelor's scores in STEM fields for a PG Diploma in AI. However, program structure and specialisations differ - an IIIT Bangalore AI ML course covers more applied sub-domains, whereas others provide a more generalist curriculum. Program durations stretch up to 2 years for some colleges, while others offer accelerated models, like our 1-year PG Diploma in Machine Learning and Artificial Intelligence by IIIT-B. 19 . When does a new batch start? New batch starts at the start of every month. However, you will start getting access to the preparatory content 7-14 days prior to the batch start date. 20 . By combining Generative AI workflows, no-code automation, and modern AI tools, professionals can automate reporting, research, email drafting, document analysis, and cross-functional business processes. The "AI-Native Professional: Workflows and Agents for Productivity" program is a structured 6-week online AI agents course with certificate designed to help professionals move from basic AI usage to confidently using AI tools, building practical workflows, and automating repetitive business processes. As the program progresses, you'll also be introduced to AI agents as an advanced automation capability. I have a full-time job. Can I realistically complete an AI automation course without it taking over my personal life? Yes, this program is delivered entirely online through a combination of live expert sessions and project work. You should expect to spend approximately 4-5 hours per week. What happens if I miss a live session? All live sessions are recorded and made available within 24 hours . While live attendance is recommended for the "build-along" experience, recordings allow you to stay on track. How long will I have access to the materials? You will retain access to all learning and project files for one year after graduation. Additionally, you will receive curriculum updates even after your term ends to stay current with the latest AI tools. Will I receive a certificate? Yes. Upon successful completion, you will earn a Professional Certificate from Great Learning. How is this AI program different from an AI automation certification course? The "AI-Native Professional: Workflows and Agents for Productivity" program differentiates itself from typical courses in several key ways: Focus on Practical AI Productivity and Workflow Automation : Build practical workflows that automate research, reporting, communication, and content creation. "Portfolio Over Paper" (Build-First Philosophy) : The program emphasizes that a tangible portfolio is more valuable to employers than a credential alone. Because the curriculum follows a "build-first" approach, you are required to create and submit functional weekly deliverables. Multi-Tool Orchestration : Rather than focusing on a single platform, you'll learn how to combine leading Generative AI tools such as ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini Notebook, Perplexity, Gamma, and Activepieces to build production ready workflows. Transferable Frameworks : Because AI tools evolve rapidly, the course prioritizes foundational methodologies over fleeting features. You will learn cross-platform frameworks, such as the Task-Context-References prompting model and strict hallucination detection workflows, ensuring your skills don't become outdated when current tools change. View more Faculty, Curriculum, and Projects Who will be teaching the program? You'll learn through weekly live mentoring sessions conducted by industry experts. The program curriculum has been designed and curated by Dr. Pavankumar Gurazada , Director of Academics at Great Learning, ensuring a structured, practical, and industry-relevant learning experience. Which AI tools should working professionals learn, and how do ChatGPT and Activepieces work together in everyday workflows? In this AI workflow automation course, you will learn a "tool-agnostic" approach, meaning you will not be locked into a single ecosystem. Instead, you will gain hands-on experience with some of the best AI automation tools used across industries: Prompting and Drafting : ChatGPT, Claude, Copilot and Gemini. Research and Reporting : ChatGPT, Claude and Gemini. Analysis and Presentation : ChatGPT, Claude and Gamma. Automation and Agents : Activepieces, Claude, ChatGPT, Google Sheets, Google Forms and Gmail. These tools help you automate research, reporting, document analysis, communication, and cross-functional workflows while improving day-to-day productivity. How do I build a portfolio in 6 weeks? Over the 6 weeks, your portfolio grows progressively as you complete hands-on projects: Week 1 : You will build a leadership brief from four messy files, using a clear 3-part prompt and checking the output line by line for wrong answers. Week 2 : You will build a weekly briefing that researches itself on a schedule, using named sources and citations you have verified. Week 3 : You will produce a spreadsheet analysis and a board deck that reconcile to the source, with every number traceable to a cell. Week 4 : You will build a complaint or inbox triage flow that runs end to end, keeps risky steps as drafts, and flags when it fails. Week 5 : You will build a reusable shortlist or reconciliation assistant with memory, one that can run without you. The core piece of your portfolio is the Week 6 Demo Day project , where you present a working automation or assistant built for a real problem in your own work. What are the specific requirements for the capstone project? The specific requirements for the capstone project emphasize building a practical, working application rather than a theoretical paper. Here are the specific requirements and expectations for the project: Solve a Real-World Problem : The core requirement is that your project must solve a real, recurring pain point or task in your own professional, academic, or personal life. Build a Functioning Multi-Step System : You must create a live, multi-step automated workflow or AI system. You will use the automation skills and triggers you learn in Week 4 as the foundation for developing this final project. Deliver a Live Demonstration : You are required to present your finalized project on "Demo Day." Follow the Development Timeline : You will receive the capstone brief in Week 4, which gives you exactly three full weeks to design and build the project. During this time, you are required to utilize structured mentor guidance to refine your project plan, tool selection, and implementation approach before presenting it to your peers and mentor. What if the usage limits or pricing models of the tools used change? We review the usage limits and pricing models for the tools used in the curriculum before every cohort. However, these may change in between, we will adapt the curriculum accordingly to accommodate those changes. View more Eligibility and Admission I have no coding background. Is this AI automation course right for me? Yes. This is an AI automation course for beginners with zero coding requirements. It is designed to help anyone start building AI workflows and agents without prior technical experience. Can HR, Marketing, or Finance professionals take this AI Agents course? Yes, the program is specifically designed for functional professionals in HR, Marketing, Finance, and Operations. Because the course has zero technical prerequisites and requires no coding, it is perfectly suited for non-technical professionals from any department. The skills you learn provide cross-functional value and are highly adaptable to your specific industry. Throughout the program, you will apply the weekly skills to your own professional context to solve real, everyday problems. When does the next cohort start? Cohorts run on a rolling schedule. Please contact a Program Advisor for exact dates and to reserve your seat. Fee and Payment What is the cost of this AI Agents course? The course fee is ₹ 50,000 + GST. Are there additional costs for the AI tools? Most tools covered have free tiers that support the coursework. Please reach out to your Program Advisor for detailed information regarding additional costs for the AI tools. How can I be sure this AI agents and workflow automation program is right for me before making a long-term commitment? You don’t have to commit to the full program upfront. You can start with Week 1 for Rs 5000 + GST. It’s a complete, standalone module where you learn how to prompt effectively, choose the right AI model for a task, spot when AI gives you a wrong answer, and see a live demo of an AI agent at work. You finish with a graded assignment, so you leave with a real, usable skill whether or not you continue. If you decide the program fits your role and goals, you move on to Weeks 2 through 6 for the remaining Rs 45000 + GST, through easy installments where you build the agents and workflows yourself. Career-related Queries Will automating my own work make me more replaceable, or is avoiding AI the bigger career risk? Avoiding AI is increasingly the bigger career risk. Automating parts of your work does not replace your value as a professional; it increases your ability to operate at a higher strategic level. The "AI-Native Professional: Workflows and Agents for Productivity" program is designed to help working professionals build practical AI workflows. Beyond the credential, you will walk away with a portfolio of working AI systems. This provides tangible proof of your "AI fluency," a skill 55% of leaders now expect as a baseline. You will also learn how to showcase these projects to hiring managers during a dedicated career guide session. You'll graduate with a portfolio of practical AI workflows and automation projects that demonstrate real business impact and workplace productivity. How do I use AI to automate tasks at work, and what will I actually build? This AI workflow automation course teaches you how to use AI tools to automate repetitive tasks and streamline daily work. You will learn how to move beyond basic AI prompts and build agent-driven workflows that connect AI models with workplace tools like Gmail, Slack, and Google Sheets. Using visual automation platforms such as Activepieces, you can create workflows with simple triggers and actions without writing code. The program also shows you how to combine multiple AI tools, such as Perplexity for live research and Gemini Notebook for document analysis, to automate reporting, research, communication, and other repetitive business tasks. With a build-first approach, you will gain hands-on experience by creating and submitting functional AI automation projects each week, helping you apply AI to real workplace scenarios. General Queries What is a Generative AI workflow? A Generative AI workflow combines AI models with automation tools so information moves automatically between applications, reducing manual work. In this program, you'll build multiple generative AI workflows that connect tools such as ChatGPT, Gemini Notebook, Gmail, Slack, Google Workspace, and Activepieces to automate everyday business tasks. Can I build automated workflows that connect Gmail, Slack, and Google Sheets without writing any code and have them run on their own while I focus on other work? Yes. Working professionals can build no-code automated workflows that connect Gmail, Slack, Google Sheets, and AI tools to handle repetitive tasks automatically. Using platforms like Activepieces and ChatGPT, you can create workflows that summarize emails, update spreadsheets, generate reports, and send Slack notifications without manual intervention. How do I start automating my work without coding? You can start automating your work without writing a single line of code by utilizing visual automation tools and plain language. The AI-Native Professional program is designed with zero technical prerequisites, making it fully accessible to professionals without any background in computing. What is the difference between AI Agents and Agentic AI? AI Agents are software systems designed to perform specific tasks such as answering questions, scheduling meetings, or retrieving information. Agentic AI goes a step further by enabling multiple AI agents to plan, reason, make decisions, and work together autonomously to achieve complex goals with minimal human intervention. In simple terms, AI Agents execute tasks, while Agentic AI manages end-to-end workflows and decision-making processes. Which AI tools should I learn first as a non-tech professional? As a non-tech professional, you should start with foundational AI tools like ChatGPT, Claude, and Gemini to learn prompting and everyday productivity workflows. Once you understand the basics, you can progress to research and knowledge tools such as Gemini Notebook and Perplexity, followed by no-code automation platforms like Activepieces and Google Workspace tools. The AI-Native Professional program's step-by-step approach helps you gradually build the skills needed to automate workflows, connect apps, and eventually create autonomous AI agents without any coding experience. Frequently asked questions about the AI, ML and Decision Science programme 1 What is the IIT Delhi Applied AI, Machine Learning and Decision Science Programme about? The Applied AI, Machine Learning and Decision Science Programme by IIT Delhi is an advanced live online executive programme designed for professionals looking to build practical expertise in Generative AI, Machine Learning, Large Language Models (LLMs), predictive analytics, and AI-powered business decision-making. Unlike traditional AI certification courses that focus only on algorithms or coding, this programme combines Applied AI with Decision Science to help learners build intelligent AI systems and translate AI insights into real business impact using optimisation, forecasting, simulation, and strategic decision frameworks. 2 What is Decision Science and why is it important today? Decision Science is the discipline that focuses on making better, structured decisions using data, analytical models, and quantitative methods. While AI and Machine Learning generate predictions and insights, Decision Science ensures these insights are translated into real‑world actions. In today’s AI‑driven business environment, organisations are not limited by their ability to build models—they are limited by their ability to make the right decisions using those models. Decision Science addresses this gap by combining predictive analytics, optimisation, simulation, and business context to drive measurable outcomes.
The Applied AI, Machine Learning and Decision Science Programme by IIT Delhi is among the very few programmes designed to build this complete, end‑to‑end capability, enabling professionals to move beyond insights to real impact. 3 Why do you need Decision Science along with AI and Machine Learning? AI and Machine Learning can identify patterns and generate predictions—but they do not decide what actions to take. Decision Science bridges this gap by helping professionals interpret AI outputs, evaluate trade-offs, and make optimal decisions in real business scenarios.For example: AI predicts demand → Decision Science helps optimise supply and inventory ML identifies customer segments → Decision Science helps allocate resources effectively Models generate insights → Decision frameworks convert them into strategic actions Batch 6 of the Applied AI, Machine Learning and Decision Science Programme from IIT Delhi combines these capabilities into a single, integrated learning journey. Unlike most programmes that focus only on AI or analytics, this programme emphasises decision-making depth alongside AI capability, making it one of the few offerings in India that brings Applied AI, ML and Decision Science together at this level of rigour and application. 4 What concepts are taught in the Applied AI, ML and Decision Science Programme? The Applied AI, ML and Decision Science Programme from IIT Delhi covers a comprehensive blend of Applied AI, Machine Learning, Generative AI, Agentic AI and decision‑science techniques. Learners work with AI‑ready data ecosystems, supervised and unsupervised ML algorithms, Deep Learning, NLP, computer vision and LLM‑based Generative AI workflows including transformers, RAG and agentic reasoning models. The programme also teaches predictive analytics, time‑series forecasting, optimisation techniques, simulation, linear and goal programming, and multi‑criteria decision‑making frameworks, providing a complete foundation for business decision science, predictive analytics certification, and AI/ML skills for working professionals. 5 Does the Applied AI, ML and Decision Science Programme include live classes by IIT Delhi faculty? Yes. The Applied AI, ML and Decision Science Programme is delivered entirely through live, interactive online sessions taught by IIT Delhi faculty members. Classes are primarily held on Saturdays from 9:30 AM to 1:00 PM, with occasional additional sessions scheduled in the afternoon when deeper coverage or extended discussions are required. A detailed session calendar will be shared with all participants well in advance to help them plan their weekly learning schedule. 6 What is the weekly time commitment for the Applied AI, ML and Decision Science Programme? Learners should expect to dedicate 6–9 hours per week to the Applied AI, ML and Decision Science Programme. This includes around 3 hours of live faculty‑led sessions and an additional 3–6 hours of self-study, such as readings, tool-based exercises, practice assignments, and preparation for quizzes. This structure ensures that learners can apply concepts gradually while balancing professional commitments. 7 Will I receive recordings of the live online sessions? Yes. Participants will have access to recordings of all live online sessions throughout the duration of the Applied AI, ML and Decision Science Programme. This allows learners to revisit lectures for revision or catch up when needed. However, since attendance contributes to programme completion requirements, learners are expected to attend most live sessions to meet academic criteria. 8 Is the IIT Delhi Applied AI, ML and Decision Science Programme suitable for working professionals? Absolutely. The programme is built specifically for working professionals, business leaders, analysts, consultants, and technology managers who want to future-proof their careers in the AI-first economy. With live weekend sessions led by IIT Delhi faculty, practical assignments, and flexible online learning, professionals can build high-demand AI and decision intelligence skills without stepping away from their current roles. 9 Do I need coding experience to enrol in the IIT Delhi Applied AI, ML and Decision Science Programme? No prior coding experience is required. The programme follows a balanced code and no-code AI learning approach, making it suitable for both technical and non-technical professionals. Participants learn foundational AI concepts through guided Python applications, intuitive no-code AI tools, machine learning workflows, and real-world business use cases designed for practical understanding rather than purely theoretical learning. 10 What certificate will I receive after completing the Applied AI, ML and Decision Science Programme? Upon meeting the academic requirements—namely a minimum of 50% attendance and 50% aggregate marks across quizzes and the capstone project—participants will receive a Certificate of Completion issued by CEP, IIT Delhi. Learners who maintain at least 40% attendance but score below 50% overall will receive a Certificate of Participation. All certificates are formally issued through IIT Delhi’s Continuing Education Programme (CEP). 11 Who evaluates the assessments, assignments and capstone projects in this programme? All academic evaluations in the Applied AI, ML and Decision Science Programme, including quizzes, assignments, examinations and capstone projects, are conducted by IIT Delhi faculty members. Evaluation follows IIT Delhi’s CEP academic standards, and faculty have full discretion regarding grading, assessment structure and any reattempt permissions. This ensures rigorous and consistent academic oversight across both Applied AI and Decision Science components. 12 What tools and technologies are covered in the Applied AI, ML and Decision Science Programme? Learners gain hands-on exposure to industry-standard tools and technologies such as Python, Tableau, Orange, Excel Solver and LINGO, along with modern Generative AI and no‑code AI platforms. These tools are used extensively in assignments, practice labs, and capstone projects, allowing participants to build practical skills across machine learning, predictive analytics, optimisation, and decision intelligence. 13 What is the eligibility for enrolling in the Applied AI, ML and Decision Science Programme? Eligibility for the Applied AI, ML and Decision Science Programme includes being a Graduate or Diploma holder (10+2+3) in any discipline. Preference is given to applicants with backgrounds in Science, Technology, Engineering, Mathematics, Management, or related quantitative fields, as the coursework involves mathematical reasoning and analytical thinking. A basic foundation in quantitative subjects helps learners fully benefit from the programme’s AI, ML and decision-science curriculum 14 Will the IIT Delhi Applied AI, ML and Decision Science Programme help me transition into AI and Generative AI roles? Yes. The programme is designed to help professionals transition into high-growth AI, Generative AI, Machine Learning, analytics, and AI-enabled decision-making roles. Learners build hands-on capability in AI model development, LLM applications, predictive analytics, optimisation frameworks, and data-driven business problem-solving — skills increasingly required across digital transformation, AI consulting, product strategy, operations, analytics, and technology leadership functions. 15 How is the IIT Delhi Applied AI, ML and Decision Science Programme different from other online AI and Generative AI courses? What are Some Frequently Asked Questions (FAQs) About this AI Leadership and Strategy Course? 1 What is AI transformation and why is it important for business leaders? AI transformation goes beyond implementing individual AI tools or experimenting with isolated use cases. It refers to the strategic integration of Artificial Intelligence into business models, decision-making processes, operations, workforce structures, customer experiences, and organisational strategy. As AI continues to reshape industries, organisations are increasingly expected to move beyond experimentation and create measurable business value from their investments. However, achieving this requires more than technology adoption. Leaders must understand how AI affects organisational capabilities, operating models, governance frameworks, and competitive advantage. For business leaders, AI transformation is becoming a strategic priority because it influences growth, productivity, innovation, customer expectations, and workforce readiness. Organisations that successfully align AI initiatives with business objectives are better positioned to create sustainable value and adapt to changing market conditions. 2 What are the timings for the weekend sessions with the domain expert for the IITM Pravartak AI Transformation in Business Programme? The timings can also change across the duration of the course to maintain the optimum programme experience. 3 How is this Executive Programme in AI Transformation for Business different from other AI programmes? Many AI programmes focus primarily on technology concepts, prompting techniques, coding, automation tools, or individual AI applications. While these topics are important, they often do not address the broader organisational challenges associated with AI adoption. The Executive Programme in AI Transformation for Business (Programme fee: ₹1,49,900 + GST / AED 6675) takes a business-first approach to AI transformation. Participants explore how AI is reshaping industries, organisations, decision-making processes, workforce structures, and operating models. The curriculum combines enterprise AI strategy, AI-powered decision making, Generative AI, Agentic AI, responsible AI governance, workforce transformation, and leadership within a single learning journey. Rather than focusing only on how AI works, the programme focuses on how leaders can create business value through AI and lead enterprise-wide transformation initiatives. 4 Who should enrol in this AI leadership course for senior executives by IITM Pravartak? This programme is designed for business leaders, transformation professionals, functional heads, product leaders, digital leaders, entrepreneurs, and senior managers with minimum 5 years of work experience who want to develop a deeper understanding of AI's business impact. It is particularly valuable for professionals responsible for strategic planning, transformation initiatives, innovation, operational excellence, customer experience, workforce management, and organisational performance. Participants do not need technical expertise or coding experience to benefit from the programme. The curriculum is structured to help leaders understand how AI can support decision-making, improve business outcomes, create competitive advantage, and prepare organisations for the future of work. 5 What will participants learn in this enterprise AI strategy course by IITM Pravartak? Participants will develop a comprehensive understanding of how AI can be leveraged to drive business transformation. The programme covers topics such as enterprise AI strategy, AI-powered decision making, data foundations, business intelligence, Generative AI, Agentic AI, responsible AI governance, workforce transformation, and organisational change. Participants will also learn how to evaluate AI opportunities, prioritise use cases, design AI operating models, assess organisational readiness, manage AI-related risks, and build transformation roadmaps aligned with business objectives. The programme culminates in an AI Transformation Blueprint that allows participants to apply their learning to a practical organisational challenge. 6 What is enterprise AI strategy and why does it matter? Enterprise AI strategy refers to the structured approach organisations use to identify, prioritise, govern, and scale AI initiatives across business functions. Without a clear strategy, organisations often struggle to move beyond isolated AI pilots and achieve meaningful business outcomes. An enterprise AI strategy helps leaders align AI investments with business goals, evaluate opportunities, allocate resources effectively, manage risks, and create a roadmap for adoption. As AI becomes a key driver of competitive advantage, organisations increasingly require leaders who can bridge the gap between technology capabilities and business priorities. 7 How can AI improve business decision-making? AI-powered decision making uses data, analytics, machine learning, and intelligent systems to support strategic and operational decisions. Organisations can use AI to improve forecasting, identify patterns, predict outcomes, optimise resource allocation, manage risks, and uncover insights that may be difficult to detect through traditional methods. AI can also help leaders reduce uncertainty, improve responsiveness, and make more informed decisions. This programme explores how AI-powered decision making can be applied across functions such as finance, operations, human resources, customer experience, and business strategy. 8 How does AI affect workforce transformation? AI is reshaping how work is performed across industries and functions. Some activities are becoming automated, while others are being augmented by AI technologies. At the same time, entirely new roles and skill requirements are emerging. Organisations need to prepare for these changes by developing workforce transformation strategies that address reskilling, capability building, organisational design, leadership development, and human-AI collaboration. This executive AI transformation in business programme explores how leaders can navigate workforce transformation while ensuring long-term organisational resilience and competitiveness. 9 What practical exposure will participants receive during the programme? Participants will engage with business-focused applications of AI through live online sessions, case discussions, applied learning activities, and the AI Transformation Blueprint capstone project. The programme also includes exposure to AI business tools, practical frameworks, industry examples, and transformation scenarios that help participants understand how AI can be applied across strategy, operations, decision-making, governance, and workforce transformation. The emphasis is on translating concepts into actionable business outcomes. 10 Why is AI leadership becoming a critical capability for senior executives? AI is increasingly influencing strategy, operations, customer experience, workforce planning, and competitive positioning. As a result, leaders can no longer treat AI as a purely technical topic. Senior executives are expected to make informed decisions about AI investments, oversee governance, manage organisational change, identify strategic opportunities, and prepare their organisations for an AI-driven future. Developing AI leadership capabilities enables professionals to navigate uncertainty, lead transformation initiatives, and position their organisations for long-term success in an increasingly AI-enabled business environment. 11 How can organisations prepare for successful AI transformation? Successful AI transformation requires more than technology investments. Organisations must align AI initiatives with business objectives, establish governance frameworks, prepare the workforce, build data capabilities, redesign operating models, and create a culture that supports innovation and change. Leaders play a critical role in guiding these efforts and ensuring that AI adoption generates measurable business value. This programme provides frameworks and tools to help participants approach AI transformation in a structured and sustainable manner. Early registrations are encouraged. Seats fill up quickly! Module 3: Prompt Engineering, Evaluation and Reliability Zero-shot and few-shot prompting, chain-of-thought reasoning, tool-aware prompting Retrieval-aware prompting, system prompts, safety prompts, hallucination mitigation Prompt templates, prompt versioning LLM evaluation frameworks; LLM-as-judge, pairwise comparison, critic-creator loop Golden datasets, RAGAS/DeepEval eval stack, reliability testing Skills Acquired: Prompt design | Evaluation methodology | LLM-as-judge | RAGAS/DeepEval | Golden dataset construction Learning Outcome: You stop guessing whether your prompts work. You measure it and you know how to improve what you measure. 3 Pillar 3: Enterprise RAG and Retrieval Infrastructure Module 4: Retrieval Architecture and Vector Infrastructure RAG fundamentals, embedding models: OpenAI/BGE/Nomic Semantic similarity, chunking strategies Vector databases: Qdrant/FAISS/Chroma, HNSW and IVF indexing Metadata enrichment, ingestion pipelines, hybrid retrieval systems Knowledge lifecycle management, PII detection and redaction Skills Acquired: Vector DB setup | Embedding selection | Chunking | Ingestion pipelines | PII handling Learning Outcome: You can take a company's document library and turn it into a retrieval system that actually finds the right thing. Module 5: Production RAG and Retrieval Optimisation BM25 and dense retrieval, reranking models: Cross-encoder Query rewriting, HyDE retrieval, multi-query retrieval Semantic caching, context compression Groundedness evaluation: RAGAS/DeepEval/TruLens, precision@K RAG failure taxonomy : retrieval vs generation vs prompt, retrieval debugging Skills Acquired: Hybrid retrieval | Reranking | HyDE | RAGAS/DeepEval | RAG failure analysis Learning Outcome: When your RAG system gives a wrong answer, you know exactly why and you know how to fix it. 4 Pillar 4: Model Adaaptation and Fine-Tuning Module 6: Fine-Tuning Strategy and Adaptation Frameworks Prompting vs. RAG vs. fine-tuning: choosing the right approach for different use cases Dataset curation and instruction tuning for domain-specific AI applications Domain adaptation and synthetic data generation for model improvement Baseline evaluation, model selection, and tuned vs. base model comparison Cost, performance, and risk analysis for AI model customization Identifying when fine-tuning is the wrong choice and selecting better alternatives Skills Acquired: Decision frameworks | Dataset curation | Instruction tuning | Synthetic data generation | Model benchmarking Learning Outcome: You can walk into a meeting and give a clear answer to "should we fine-tune this?" backed by a framework, not a gut feeling. Module 7: Parameter-Efficient Model Adaptation LoRA, QLoRA, PEFT frameworks, quantization, adapter architectures Training workflows, hyperparameter tuning, dataset formatting Model evaluation, serving fine-tuned models HuggingFace PEFT/TRL, bitsandbytes, Unsloth/Axolotl Catastrophic forgetting, GPU/Colab lab path Skills Acquired: LoRA/QLoRA implementation | PEFT/TRL | Quantization | Model serving | HuggingFace ecosystem Learning Outcome: You fine-tune an open-source model on your own data, on a single GPU, and deploy it as an API you can call. 5 Pillar 5: Agentic AI and Autonomous Workflows Module 8: Agent Architecture, Tooling and Memory Systems ReAct architecture, tool-calling agents, API orchestration, function calling Planning loops, memory systems, vector memory, retrieval-as-a-tool Grounded agents, text-to-SQL agents Failure-Oriented Design: transient/permanent/silent/cascading/adversarial failures Max-iteration guards, circuit breakers, prompt-injection defense Skills Acquired: ReAct | Tool/function calling | Memory architecture | Text-to-SQL | Failure engineering | Injection defense Learning Outcome: You build an agent that uses real tools, handles failures gracefully, and doesn't go rogue when something unexpected happens. Module 9: Agent Orchestration and Human Oversight LangGraph workflows, state-machine orchestration, planner-executor systems Reflection loops, self-correction systems HITL workflows, approval gates, escalation systems, audit trails Streaming UX ; tool-call streaming, reasoning streaming, interruptibility Skills Acquired: LangGraph | HITL design | Reflection loops | Audit trails | Streaming agent UX Learning Outcome: You can design a workflow where a human stays in the loop at the right moments and the system knows when to ask. Module 10: Multi-Agent Coordination Systems Multi-agent architectures, supervisor-worker systems, task delegation Shared state management, inter-agent communication, coordination failures Distributed workflows, cost and latency optimisation When NOT to use multi-agent systems Skills Acquired: Supervisor-worker design | Shared state | Coordination failure handling | Multi-agent cost engineering Learning Outcome: You coordinate a team of agents working on a task together and you know when one agent is the smarter call. 6 Pillar 6: AI Infrastructure, Security, Governance and Deployment Module 11: MCP Protocols, AI Security and Governance MCP architecture, SSE and stdio transport Retrieval poisoning, tool abuse vulnerabilities, data exfiltration risks AI guardrails: Guardrails AI, NeMo Guardrails, permission management GDPR and DPDP compliance, enterprise AI governance, audit trails Skills Acquired: MCP server setup | AI guardrails | Prompt injection defense | GDPR/DPDP compliance | Governance frameworks Learning Outcome: You can tell your CTO: this AI system is secure, auditable, and compliant with India's DPDP rules. Module 12: AI Deployment, Observability and Runtime Operations Logging, tracing and metrics ; Langfuse Distributed tracing, cost observability, token tracking Semantic caching for cost, FastAPI deployment CI/CD for AI systems; GitHub Actions, regression testing Prompt versioning, model routing; runtime fallback mechanisms Skills Acquired: Langfuse | Cost engineering | Model routing | Fallback design Learning Outcome: Your AI system is live, monitored, and you get alerted before the user does when something goes wrong. Module 13: Capstone Project Architecture design, RAG integration, agent workflow implementation Fine-tuned model integration, deployment pipeline setup Skills Acquired: AI system design | RAG and agent integration | Fine-tuned model deployment | Production monitoring Learning Outcome: Graduate with a production-ready AI system integrating RAG, agents, and fine-tuned models. What Hands-on Exercises Will You Complete in the Agentic AI and RAG Systems Programme? Every module in this programme connects directly to a hands-on project. Each project builds on the last, progressively developing the capability that culminates in your capstone. 1 Project 01 | Prompt Lab: Compare LLM Strategies on a Task Week 6 | Foundation Models and LLM Engineering You take one real task and solve it three ways — zero-shot, few-shot, and structured chain-of-thought. You score each strategy against a golden dataset using an LLM-as-judge evaluation and write up which approach won and why. You walk away knowing how to measure prompt quality not just feel it. You will build: A notebook or CLI with evaluation results and a written comparison of which prompting strategy performed best and why. 2 Project 02 | Mini-RAG: Ask Your Documents Week 9 | Enterprise RAG and Retrieval Infrastructure You build your first end-to-end RAG pipeline from scratch over a corpus you choose. Load, chunk, embed, store, retrieve, and generate answers grounded in what you put in. The first time it actually works on a document you uploaded yourself is a different feeling from a tutorial. You will build: A working end-to-end RAG pipeline from document ingestion to grounded answer generation. 3 Project 03 | Grounded Q&A: A Cited Document Assistant Week 12 | Production RAG and Retrieval Optimisation You take Mini-RAG further add hybrid retrieval, a reranker, inline source citations, and confident abstention when the answer isn't supported. Then you measure it: hit rate and precision@K on a real question set. This is where RAG stops being a demo. You will build: A production-ready document assistant with citations, abstention, hybrid retrieval, and a retrieval quality report. 4 Project 04 | Specialise a Model: Fine-Tune a Small LLM Week 14 | Model Adaptation and Fine-Tuning You take a small open-source model — Llama, Mistral, or Phi-class, curate a dataset for one narrow task, and run a QLoRA fine-tune on a GPU. Then you evaluate the tuned model against the base model and write a decision log: when was fine-tuning the right call and when wasn't it. You will build: A fine-tuned open-source model with evaluation results and a written decision log. 5 Project 05 | Tool-Using Agent: A Task Assistant That Acts Week 20 | Agentic AI and Autonomous Workflows You build a single agent that plans and uses two or three real tools — document search, calculator, SQL lookup. You implement a visible reasoning trace with max-iteration guards and failure fallback. The optional extension: a small planner-worker-reviewer crew with clear roles and handoffs. You will build: A working tool-calling agent with a visible reasoning trace, iteration guards, and failure fallback — deployed and callable. 6 Project 06 | Connected Assistant: Integrate a Tool via MCP Week 21 | AI Infrastructure, Security and Governance You connect an assistant to an external data source through an MCP server building or connecting a small custom server and securing it with an allow-list or input validation. This is the architecture pattern behind every serious enterprise AI integration happening right now. You will build: A live MCP-connected assistant with a secured, exposed tool; callable, demonstrable, and ready to extend. What is the Capstone Project in the Agentic AI and RAG Systems Programme? Over six months, build and deploy a production-ready Agentic AI and RAG system that integrates retrieval, intelligent agents, monitoring, and deployment.
